raw_response:
I am old now, but I still do not farm blindly. On 12 mu with only two people in the household, I have to keep the plan practical and steady. Wheat-maize is still my backbone because it spreads risk across the year and keeps land productive. Cotton I will keep on a smaller area, because it needs more attention and more hand labor at picking time. I have well water, so I am not completely dependent on rain, but pumping costs money, so I only irrigate at the key stages. I have enough experience to know that cutting fertilizer too much is risky in Quzhou, especially for wheat, but on a small household farm I also do not chase the maximum possible yield. I aim for a stable harvest and manageable labor. For wheat, I will use a moderate-high base fertilizer and one topdress, with about three irrigations if spring stays dry. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize immediately on that same land with simple land preparation, because the turnaround window is very short. On cotton, I will not push inputs as hard as on grain land; I will keep fertilizer moderate and watch insects carefully, because cotton can lose profit quickly if pests get ahead of me. That is how I think this year: stable grain first, cotton as supplementary income, and no unnecessary spending.
